candidates.title: The emulator build and its Docker image reuse stale generated uarch files, so the uarch program and pristine hash (and the on-chain UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH that machine-solidity-step generates from that image) can come from older sources than the native interpreter and MARCHID built with them
candidates.component: Emulator build and release: src/Makefile (generate-uarch-pristine), the top-level Makefile (all -> source-default), Dockerfile with .dockerignore (the image cartesi/machine-emulator:devel), and the machine-solidity-step generate-constants path that builds and queries that image
candidates.role: Referee verifier, for the UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH and CM_MARCHID that machine-solidity-step's generate-constants takes from the image (AUDIT.md: 'machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1, with its generated code and constants regenerated from audit/prt2 | Referee verifier'). Honest operator, for the uarch program embedded in the emulator (AUDIT.md row 'uarch program ... | Honest operator').
candidates.location: src/Makefile:668-675 (`../uarch/uarch-pristine-ram.c ../uarch/uarch-pristine-hash.c: generate-uarch-pristine`, and generate-uarch-pristine runs the uarch build only `ifeq (,$(wildcard ../uarch/uarch-pristine-hash.c))`); src/Makefile:641-645 (uarch-pristine-*.o compiled from whatever .c exists); src/Makefile:614 (cm-version.h, hence MARCHID, IS regenerated when src/Makefile changes); Makefile:178 and 309-310 (`all` runs only `make -C src`); .dockerignore:8-9 (`**/*.bin` then `!uarch/uarch-ram.bin`, with no pattern excluding uarch/uarch-pristine-ram.c or uarch-pristine-hash.c); Dockerfile:63-64 (`COPY . .` then `make`) and :69 (`make install-uarch` ships uarch/uarch-ram.bin from the context). machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1 helper_scripts/generate_EmulatorConstants.sh:21-31 (runs `make build-emulator-image` in EMULATOR_DIR, then reads cartesi.UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH and cartesi.MARCHID from cartesi/machine-emulator:devel), while generate-step (Makefile:116) reads EMULATOR_DIR/src/uarch-step.cpp directly.
candidates.description: The uarch program is a generated artifact of interpret.cpp and its headers, which uarch/Makefile compiles into uarch-ram.bin. That binary is then embedded in the emulator as uarch-pristine-ram.c, with its hash in uarch-pristine-hash.c. Both files are untracked (uarch/.gitignore). The emulator's own build never refreshes them once they exist. generate-uarch-pristine invokes the uarch build only when uarch-pristine-hash.c is absent, and the top-level `make` builds only src. So any build in a tree that has built the uarch once, after a change to the interpreter or after a checkout of another commit (untracked files survive checkout), does three things. (1) It recompiles the native interpreter from the new sources. (2) It regenerates cm-version.h, and with it MARCHID, whenever src/Makefile changed. (3) It links the old uarch image and the old pristine hash unchanged. Nothing detects the mismatch. The embedded pristine hash still equals the hash of the embedded image, so the collector's 'microarchitecture is not pristine' check, reset_uarch, and the player's comparison of cartesi.UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH with the verifier all pass. The Docker image has the same defect. .dockerignore sends uarch/uarch-pristine-ram.c, uarch-pristine-hash.c and, by an explicit exception, uarch/uarch-ram.bin into the build context. The `make` inside the image then reuses them, and `make install-uarch` packages the stale uarch-ram.bin into the .deb. machine-solidity-step's documented generate-constants path builds exactly this image from the developer's EMULATOR_DIR working tree. It takes UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH (the hash that UArchReset writes on-chain) and CM_MARCHID from the image, but takes UArchStep.sol from the working tree's src/uarch-step.cpp. The verifier constants fixed on-chain therefore depend on unaudited, untracked files rather than on the audited source. The result can be a verifier with the new CM_MARCHID 23 and an old pristine hash. It can also be an emulator whose native interpreter (mcycle claims) and uarch (uarch claims, on-chain step) implement different instruction semantics, for example the timer, failed-SC, page-walk and sip changes of commits 0dfebe1, 2175acb, de2a679 and 75e9f89 that this branch made after the previous release. CI builds from fresh checkouts and is not affected. The bugs/harness Docker build avoided the problem only by replacing the repository's .dockerignore with one that excludes generated files.
candidates.trigger: No adversary is needed. The trigger is a maintainer or deployer who builds the emulator, or runs machine-solidity-step's `make generate-constants` or `make build`, from a working tree where `make` (or `make uarch`) ran at an earlier commit. A realistic case: a tree built at v0.23.0-test2 or at any commit before 0dfebe1, then updated to audit/prt2 and used to regenerate the step. The adversary can only exploit a resulting deployment.
candidates.reachability: Deterministic whenever the generated uarch files predate the current interpreter sources. A `git pull`, `git checkout`, or local edit followed by `make` or `make build-emulator-image` is the ordinary workflow, and the step generator's own Makefile runs `make build-emulator-image` in that tree. Shown with `make -n` on a git-archive copy of HEAD that holds dated generated files: the plan compiles the stale uarch-pristine-*.c into libcartesi.a and never invokes the uarch build. Without those files, the same target runs `make -C .. uarch`.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: no. The trigger is building the emulator, image and verifier constants from the project's own Makefiles and Dockerfile. It needs no untrusted API caller, untrusted snapshot, host fault or reorganization. The exclusion 'Defects that need the deployment to violate one of A1 to A8, unless the emulator's own behavior is what makes the obligation fail' does not apply, because the emulator's build is what makes A6 ('Every verifier, the uarch program fixed on-chain, and every honest operator in a deployment implements the same state transition function (R13)') fail silently. 2. Role: the generated on-chain constants are in the Referee verifier row of AUDIT.md ('with its generated code and constants regenerated from audit/prt2'), and the uarch program is in the Honest operator row. The most critical role is Referee verifier. No support cap applies. 3. High and Medium cases: High, 'A uarch program or verifier code fixed on-chain that cannot be reproducibly rebuilt, while what is deployed matches its audited source.' The rule is R13: 'The uarch program, its pristine hash, and the verifier code that a deployment fixes on-chain must be reproducibly buildable from audited source.' The documented build path, including the step's generate-constants, produces an output that depends on untracked files in the tree rather than on the audited source, and it gives no error. 4. Critical: only if a stale build is actually deployed or run by an honest node. Native and uarch interpretation then disagree at reachable states on every changed instruction, which violates R2 ('Native interpretation. The uarch running the interpreter, plus the uarch reset ... must agree'). That is a completeness failure of section 1: the honest mcycle claim, computed natively, cannot be backed by uarch-level proofs that the on-chain verifier accepts. Rated Critical then. 5. Low: under the reading that a clean checkout (which CI uses) is enough for 'reproducibly buildable', no rule is violated until a stale build is used, and the defect is Low build hygiene. The deciding fact is whether the generate-constants path of machine-solidity-step, which builds the image from a developer working tree, counts as how the verifier fixed on-chain is built.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (High under the reading that the step generator's documented image build is how the on-chain constants are built, like R1-R13-1; Low if only clean-checkout CI builds count; Critical if a stale build is deployed)
candidates.threat_to_goal: A verifier or emulator built this way implements a mixed protocol version. Its CM_MARCHID and native interpreter are new, while its uarch program and on-chain pristine hash are old. The only version check the recipes make (pristine hash, R1-A6-2) passes, because both sides come from the same stale build. The honest operator's natively computed mcycle claim can then disagree with what its uarch and the on-chain step reproduce at a disputed position. The honest claim loses a leaf match it should win, which is the completeness failure of section 1. It is the same root cause as R1-R13-1: a generated protocol artifact drifts from the emulator source and no check covers it.
candidates.evidence: (a) Read src/Makefile:668-675, uarch/.gitignore, .dockerignore, Dockerfile:63-69, and the step's generate_EmulatorConstants.sh:21-31. (b) Ran `make -n -W interpret.cpp` in src/ of the real tree, changing nothing: it rebuilds interpret.o, libcartesi.a and cartesi.so, links uarch-pristine-ram.o and uarch-pristine-hash.o unchanged, and never invokes the uarch build. (c) In a scratch `git archive HEAD src uarch tools Makefile` copy, with dated sentinel uarch/uarch-pristine-{hash,ram}.c, `make -n -C src libcartesi.a` compiles the sentinels into the library. `make -n -C src generate-uarch-pristine` prints no uarch build. After deleting the sentinels, it prints `make -C .. uarch` / `uarch-with-toolchain`. (d) A Python reimplementation of the .dockerignore matching (scripts/dockerignore.py in the scratch dir) reports uarch/uarch-pristine-hash.c, uarch/uarch-pristine-ram.c, uarch/uarch-ram.bin, src/cm-version.h and src/interpret-jump-table.hpp as SENT to the build context, while *.o and *.a are excluded. (e) The harness README notes that its own image build uses a Dockerfile-specific .dockerignore 'so images never pick up in-tree build outputs'.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh, with no build and no docker daemon needed for part 1. (1) `git archive HEAD src uarch tools Makefile` into a temp dir. Write sentinel uarch/uarch-pristine-hash.c and uarch-pristine-ram.c dated 2020-01-01, older than src/interpret.cpp. Run `make -n -C src libcartesi.a`. Assert that the plan either rebuilds the uarch (mentions `make -C .. uarch`, `uarch-with-toolchain` or `uarch-ram.elf`) or refuses to proceed. Today it compiles the sentinels, so exit 1. (2) Assert that the repository's .dockerignore excludes uarch/uarch-pristine-*.c and uarch/uarch-ram.bin from the context, using a matcher or `docker build` of a 'FROM scratch / COPY uarch/uarch-pristine-hash.c /' Dockerfile over the temp copy with the repository's .dockerignore. Today the COPY succeeds, so exit 1. A fix (make the generated files depend on the uarch sources, or always build the uarch through uarch/Makefile, and exclude generated uarch files from the Docker context) makes both pass.

candidates.title: The uarch 'validate-instruction-set' guard fails open: grep -w accepts any dotted mnemonic (c.add, fence.i, ...) and the extraction regex drops undecodable encodings (.word/.insn), so the build cannot catch uarch code that UArchStep does not implement
candidates.component: uarch program build: uarch/Makefile targets uarch-ram.elf.insn.txt and validate-instruction-set
candidates.role: Honest operator (AUDIT.md: 'uarch program'). The guard protects the uarch program that the referee verifier must implement.
candidates.location: uarch/Makefile:33-35 (SUPPORTED_UARCH_INSN), :161-162 (`grep -oP '^\s*[0-9a-f]{4,8}\:\s+[0-9a-f]{4,8}\s+\K[a-z]\S+'`, which only captures mnemonics starting with [a-z]), :164-165 (`objdump -M no-aliases -d`), :167-172 (`grep -v -w -E "$(SUPPORTED_UARCH_INSN)"`).
candidates.description: validate-instruction-set exists to guarantee that the uarch binary contains only the RV64I instructions that uarch-step.cpp, and therefore the generated UArchStep.sol, implements. Any other instruction is a uarch trap ('illegal instruction'), which R3 calls Critical from a reachable state. The check has two fail-open gaps. (1) `grep -w` treats '.' as a word boundary, so a mnemonic such as `c.add`, `c.ld` or `fence.i` matches the listed word `add`, `ld` or `fence` and is accepted. uarch-step.cpp decodes no compressed instruction and treats funct3=1 (fence.i) as illegal. (2) The extraction regex keeps only mnemonics that start with a lowercase letter. objdump prints encodings outside the ELF's merged arch attribute as `.word`/`.insn`, and those lines are silently dropped. For example, `mul` in an object whose attribute does not include M disassembles as `.word 0x02b50533`. The shipped binary is fine: the pinned toolchain has an rv64i/lp64 multilib, and today's insn.txt holds only the 52 supported mnemonics. But the guard does not deliver what it promises for any toolchain or source change that brings in compressed, dotted or undecodable encodings. Examples are a libgcc multilib fallback with C, inline `.insn`/`.word`, or a `__builtin___clear_cache` that emits fence.i.
candidates.trigger: A build with a toolchain or source change that puts such an instruction in uarch-ram.elf. No adversary. A guest can only exploit a resulting binary, by steering execution to that code (a uarch trap from a reachable state).
candidates.reachability: Not reachable with the pinned toolchain and current sources. Verified that the libgcc used for -march=rv64i -mabi=lp64 is the rv64i/lp64 multilib and that uarch-ram.elf has no 16-bit instructions. The gap is in the check, which passes on a crafted ELF.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: no exclusion fits. It is a build-time guard of the uarch program, triggered by building. 2. Role: uarch program, Honest operator. 3. High and Medium cases: none fits. The uarch program fixed on-chain can be rebuilt from audited source and today contains no unsupported instruction, so the High case 'A uarch program ... that cannot be reproducibly rebuilt' does not apply. 4. Critical: no rule is violated at a reachable state with the shipped binary. R3 ('A pristine uarch program must never trap from a reachable state') would be violated only by a binary that the broken guard lets through. 5. Low: 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model'. It is a verification gap in the build of a protocol artifact, from the same family as R1-R13-1 (generated artifacts that drift from what the verifier implements, with no check to catch it).
candidates.threat_to_goal: None today. If the binary ever contains a compressed, fence.i or undecodable instruction, the guard reports success. Every main-processor step that executes that uarch code then traps in the uarch, and the on-chain UArchStep reverts with 'illegal instruction'. The honest operator cannot prove its transition, which is a completeness failure (R3 and R4).
candidates.evidence: Assembled t.S in the pinned toolchain image (cartesi/machine-emulator:toolchain, gcc 14.2.0), with -march=rv64i_zifencei, containing add, fence.i, c.add (via .option arch,+c), .word 0x0000000b, .word 0x02b50533 (mul) and ecall. The objdump with -M no-aliases shows `fence.i`, `c.add`, `.word ...`, `.insn 2, 0x0001`. The Makefile's exact extraction regex yields insn.txt = {add, c.add, ecall, fence.i}. The Makefile's exact `grep -v -w -E "$(SUPPORTED_UARCH_INSN)"` reports nothing, so the check passes. Files: scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARGEN/insncheck/{t.S,run.sh}. Also confirmed: `riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64i -mabi=lp64 -print-libgcc-file-name` gives .../rv64i/lp64/libgcc.a, and uarch-ram.elf.objdump has no 16-bit instructions.
candidates.test_idea: A test.sh that builds (or ships as a fixture) a tiny RISC-V ELF containing c.add, fence.i and a .word encoding, runs the Makefile's own uarch-ram.elf.insn.txt and validate-instruction-set recipes on it (`make -C uarch validate-instruction-set` with the objdump file overridden), and asserts the check fails. Today it passes, so exit 1. A fix matches whole lines (grep -x) and treats any line not starting with a supported mnemonic, '.word'/'.insn' included, as unsupported.

not_covered: Did not rebuild the emulator, the uarch or the step to demonstrate a stale-uarch build end to end (the rules forbid rebuilding the shared harness). The evidence for candidate 1 is make -n on the real tree and on a git-archive copy, plus .dockerignore matching. No docker build of the repository context was run, because the context would include bugs/harness/work (tens of GB).

Emulator DTB cmio/yield nodes. cm.cpp static_asserts tie cm.h constants to the C++ definitions, and UARCH_CYCLE_MAX is derived from ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_UARCH_CYCLES_PER_MCYCLE.

Not pursued, possible A7 drift: Dave's released clock constants (docs/measurements/constants.md: COMMITMENT_BUDGET and the [38,0]/[54,38] table) were derived on emulator 0.21.0 (macOS, density 566 usteps per big cycle, leaf rate 173/s), and dimensioning.md cites v0.21 and v0.22 figures. Did not measure this branch's uarch density or bulk collector rate against them; that is R1-A7-1 territory.

Not reported (dropped earlier or out of my angle): prt-lua-bridge.md's claim that the release's machine/step matches the emulator's pristine state (R1-A6-3, dropped); the CM_MARCHID check gap (R1-A6-2); the src/Makefile's independent UARCH_PRISTINE_RAM_C/HASH_C overrides (custom-pristine builds only); machine-solidity-step's test-replay downloading logs of the released v0.23.0-test2 emulator (a test-data drift, excluded as missing tests); the yield tool's mode/reason mixing.

Not covered: Dave's Rust/sling node and the Cartesi Rollups Node (out of scope); the JSON-RPC discover/schema files and Lua JSON schemas as protocol artifacts; MachineValidityProof/OutputValidityProof ABI encoding in prt-ethereum.lua (support; the demo settles); rollup-http-server's output encoding; the reproducibility of the guest-tools rootfs binaries against the tag source; outputs larger than a transaction can carry (A5/R12, noted only).
